cards.lore: Triggers Bradykinin (Cough). Watch for Angio-Edema-Annie & hyperkalemia.
cards.gradeReason: Character is vivid but bradykinin/Angio-Edema lore demands prior knowledge.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Pen-and-ink cartoon. Subject: Armored elephant crushing blood-pressure pipes. Mood: Industrial, weighty.

cards.lore: Targeted at vessels, not the heart. Causes Edema-Eddie (swollen ankles).

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Warm cartoon illustration. Subject: Polar bear firefighter relaxing calcium channels in pipes. Mood: Cool, industrial.

cards.lore: High-potency. Steals potassium (Hypo-K-Karl) and risks Oto-Toxic-Oliver at high doses.
cards.gradeReason: Flood-Gate opens, K+ vanishes, ears ring — three facts, one performance.

cards.lore: No INR monitoring. Hard to reverse (needs Andexxa). Renal failure toxicity.
cards.gradeReason: Andexxa reversal is too specialist; card describes without giving a student a handle.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Bold graphic. Subject: Walrus blocking a giant glowing Factor Xa portal. Mood: Imposing, futuristic.

cards.gradeReason: Sugar-Stopper is solid; Lactic-Lucy is memorable but the renal caveat needs context.

cards.gradeReason: Key-into-cell is the perfect mnemonic; Final-Boss framing commands respect immediately.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Regal cartoon. Subject: Lion king sleeping on cloud of pain-relief, constipated courtier nearby. Mood: Majestic, drowsy.

cards.lore: Eats the stomach (Percy-the-Ulcer) and hits the kidneys (Renal-Ray).
cards.gradeReason: Fire-Extinguisher is solid; Percy and Renal-Ray name the damage but COX nuance needs context.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Dark cartoon. Subject: Electric eel with muffler clamped on nerve channels, sleepy characters nearby. Mood: Sedated, electric.

cards.lore: Watch for Allergy-Annie and Clostrid-the-Colitis (C. diff).
cards.gradeReason: Wall-Wrecker makes beta-lactam action physical and immediate; Allergy-Annie is table lore.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Construction cartoon. Subject: Woodpecker demolishing bacterial cell wall with drill. Mood: Energetic, decisive.

cards.lore: Go-To for serious Gram+ infections. Causes Biliary-Sludge.
cards.gradeReason: Meningitis-Mauler is a strong image; Gram+ hierarchy and Biliary-Sludge need infectious disease context.

cards.lore: Superior for Percy-the-Ulcer. Long-term drops Mg²⁺ and invites C-Diff.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Plumbing cartoon. Subject: Tortoise locking acid pipeline valve with giant padlock. Mood: Decisive, relieving.

cards.gradeReason: BBB-crossing and EPS without a single hook to perform — jargon outweighs character.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Library cartoon. Subject: Owl in spectacles boosting acetylcholine signal in library, drool puddle. Mood: Brainy, parasympathetic.

cards.lore: Not for heart disease patients—it constricts all pipes!

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Night club cartoon. Subject: Gorilla bouncer calming neural crowd instantly, alcohol bottle crossed out. Mood: Authoritative, addictive.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Warm cartoon. Subject: Capybara sitting in golden serotonin reservoir, clock showing 4 weeks. Mood: Hopeful, slow-build.

cards.lore: The Lithium-Level-Check is law. Toxic to Thyroid/Renal.
cards.gradeReason: Seesaw-Stabilizer for bipolar is iconic; Lithium-Level-Check is law = three words of clinical truth.
cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Heavy cartoon. Subject: Tortoise anchoring a bipolar seesaw, thyroid and kidney warning flags. Mood: Steady, precarious.

cards.artworkPrompt: Style: Gritty cartoon. Subject: T-rex in handcuffs, stiff limbs, leaning posture — NMS rendered physically. Mood: Restrained, old-school.

cards.lore: Essential for failing hearts. Can cause Mon-Boob-Mike.

verdict: The Synaptic Arsenal is the strongest MedKayfab deck yet — 52 drug characters each carry a mechanism, a danger, and a personality, wrapped in a name that sticks (Warf-the-Old-Guard, Kay-the-Supplement, Nitro-the-Bomb). The Quest synthesis cards on the final page are a brilliant pedagogical layer that turns the deck into a clinical reasoning game. Weakness: the oncology and antiarrhythmic pages lose the playful hook and skew text-heavy. Table-ready: YES.
blurb: Fifty-six drug characters teach mechanisms, side effects, and clinical pearls through roleplay and synthesis quests. For medical students who want pharmacology to actually stick.

marketingText:
MedKayfab: PHARMACOLOGY – The Synaptic Arsenal (Medical Mnemonics Cut & Play Comic)

56 illustrated medical mnemonic cards to master drug mechanisms, narrow therapeutic windows, and the toxicities that turn a medicine into a poison.

You drew the dose from memory. The heart rate is 30, the patient describes yellow halos around the ceiling lights, and the ECG sags into a reverse tick. Nothing on this chart was an overdose. It was a dose one notch too high for a drug whose safe range is the width of a hair. In pharmacology the gap between rescue and harm is rarely the wrong molecule. It is the wrong number.

MedKayfab Pharmacology translates the invisible war of receptors, half-lives, and therapeutic windows into a narrative wrestling match. Stop memorizing drug tables. Start performing them.

YOU'LL GET
- 56 illustrated MedKayfab cards (14pp, 4 cards/page)
- Full MedKayfab Freestyle rules (Quest Die mechanics)
- S-Tier characters like Adrenal-the-All-Star, Digoxi-the-Fox, and Warf-the-Old-Guard
- Free lifetime updates as guidelines evolve
- CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 licence
- PDF optimized for home printing (A4 / Letter)

What's in the deck
You'll meet Adrenal-the-All-Star, the king of the code-blue who restarts a stalled engine and, in the same breath, can overheat it into ischemia. Digoxi-the-Fox works a window so narrow that trouble announces itself in yellow-tinted vision and a reverse-tick ECG long before a lab value catches up. Warf-the-Old-Guard anticoagulates on an INR-tether, picks food-fights with a plate of leafy greens, and stays teratogenic the moment a pregnancy walks into the room. Every character is a mechanism you can argue with instead of a row you have to recite.

How it works
Every card is a cognitive anchor designed for high-stress retrieval. You have the Character (the mnemonic), the Visual (the scene), the Stat Block (doses, windows, contraindications), the Lore (the clinical story), and the Quest (the reasoning challenge). The Mechanism Flash mode is unforgiving here: if you cannot name the drug's mechanism and its lethal edge in one sentence without looking, the patient on the Stage doesn't make it.

Honest cognitive load
This is an S-Tier core engine. It is broad and dense by design, since pharmacology touches every system in the body, which makes it a strong backbone deck for medical students heading into exams and for residents who want their dosing reflexes sharp. It pairs cleanly with Internal Medicine for the disease context, with Cardiology for the rhythm drugs Digoxi-the-Fox and Adrenal-the-All-Star live inside, and with Emergency Medicine when those same drugs get pushed under pressure.

ABOUT MEDKAYFAB
MedKayfab is a narrative medical learning card game, 50 decks covering the full medical curriculum. Every card encodes a clinical mechanism as a character with a personality, a story, and a reasoning challenge. Built by a physician. Assembled with AI tools. Manually revised. Honest about its limitations. Free to use, share, and adapt under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.

PAY WHAT YOU WANT
This deck is Pay What You Want, including free. If you find it useful, a fair price is €5. Student on a budget? Enter €0, no questions asked. Want to support more decks? Anything above fair price is appreciated. Share freely, attribute honestly, never resell.

DISCLAIMER
MedKayfab is a learning companion, not a clinical reference. Content was created by a physician and reviewed to the best of our knowledge, but medicine evolves, guidelines change, and some mechanisms in here will be simplified or wrong. Always verify against current primary sources and clinical guidelines before applying anything to patient care. The Blödsinn! is the vehicle. The science is serious.

Stay fluffy. — Doc FrizzleBob
